title: Goulash
subtitle: Hungarian beef and paprika stew
excerpt: Hungary's national dish: beef braised low and slow in a sauce built almost entirely from sweet paprika, onions, and beef stock, with caraway seeds and a finish of soured cream. Simple, deeply savoury, and a masterclass in what paprika can do when used in quantity.

recipe.sourceNotes: Goulash (gulyás in Hungarian, originally a herdsman's dish) is the national dish of Hungary and one of the defining dishes of central European cooking. Historically it was a dried, preserved preparation made by herdsmen who cooked meat with onions until the liquid evaporated, then sun-dried it and rehydrated it on the road. The modern version is a braised stew defined by its large quantity of sweet Hungarian paprika: a proper goulash uses 2 to 4 tablespoons per kilogram of meat. The paprika is added to the onions and cooked in fat for a minute before any liquid is added; this blooms the spice and removes rawness. Tomatoes, peppers, and caraway are traditional additions; soured cream is a common garnish in Hungarian and Austrian versions.

content.text: Use Hungarian sweet paprika if you can find it; the Spanish smoked variety makes a very different dish. Cook the paprika in the fat with the onions for a full minute before adding liquid; this step is not optional. The onions should be cooked very thoroughly before the paprika goes in, almost to a golden, soft jam.

items.preparation: or beef chuck; cut into 4 cm cubes

content.text: Heat the oil in a large, heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions slowly for 20 minutes until very soft and beginning to colour. Add the garlic, red peppers, and caraway seeds. Cook for 5 minutes.

Remove the pot from the heat momentarily. Add the paprika and stir into the onion mixture. Return to medium heat and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly. Add the beef and stir to coat in the paprika mixture.

Add the tinned tomatoes, stock, and bay leaves. Season. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook over very low heat for 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is completely tender. The sauce should be thick and deeply coloured. Serve with egg noodles or bread dumplings and a spoonful of soured cream.
